The image shows a Trapezoid Chest Pocket (Trapezoidal Welt Pocket) rather than a standard rectangular welt pocket. The upper and lower pocket edges are not parallel in length, creating a subtle widening toward the outer end of the chest.

Geometry

Define:

LtL_t = Top edge length
LbL_b = Bottom edge length
HH = Pocket height
α\alpha = Pocket rake angle

For a classic bespoke trapezoid chest pocket:

Top Length      = 12.0 cm
Bottom Length   = 10.5 cm
Pocket Height   = 2.5 cm
Pocket Angle    = 12°

Trapezoid Formula

Area:

A=(Lt+Lb)2HA=\frac{(L_t+L_b)}{2}H

Using the dimensions above:

A=(12.0+10.5)2(2.5)A=\frac{(12.0+10.5)}{2}(2.5) A=28.125 cm2A=28.125\text{ cm}^2

P1=(0,0)P_1=(0,0) P2=(12.0,0)P_2=(12.0,0) P3=(10.5,2.5)P_3=(10.5,2.5) P4=(0,2.5)P_4=(0,2.5)

This creates a trapezoidal shape widening toward the armhole side, matching the illustration.

Style Characteristics

A trapezoid chest pocket:

Creates a more dynamic visual line than a straight welt.
Follows the opening angle of the lapel more naturally.
Makes the chest appear slightly broader.
Is commonly used on high-end bespoke, Italian tailoring, and fashion-forward jackets.
Pairs especially well with peak lapels from 105° to 120° and shawl lapels from 10 cm to 13 cm wide.
